$comment: Build-time budgets enforced by scripts/check-build-budget (engine.py check-build-budget).
Budgets are measured with Clang -ftime-trace aggregated by ClangBuildAnalyzer;
The gate fails when a project header's average per-include parse time exceeds its
budget, or when total frontend parse time exceeds the global budget.
Rationale for avg-per-include (not total): total scales with how many TUs happen to
include a header, so it grows as the codebase grows even if the header is unchanged.
Average per-include measures the header's intrinsic weight - the thing we control.
Absolute ms are host-dependent; budgets carry deliberate headroom over the CI baseline
and are meant to catch regressions (a heavy include sneaking into a header), not to
track small run-to-run noise. Raise a budget only with a profile-build measurement and
$calibration: Budgets are calibrated to the GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 runner, not a fast local machine.
Original header baselines: log.hpp ~2240 ms, file_sink.hpp ~1660 ms, debugger_sink.hpp ~1290 ms.
The assertion-subsystem CI profile measured 73.8 s summed frontend time and 18.51 s build wall
time with the expanded test graph; all reported project headers remained within their limits.
The previous 65 s total budget was based on ~45 s before the assertion runtime and tests.
Raise only the aggregate budget to 100 s (~35% headroom over the observed 73.8 s CI run).
The shared assertion test driver also removes one duplicate compilation; no test is disabled.
This is conservative calibration from the pre-optimization CI measurement, not a claim of
post-optimization CI timing. Keep per-header limits unchanged. Evidence and local before/after

That calibration predates main's Logging redesign; current per-header limits follow

Re-measure on the CI runner before changing these budgets again.
$logging_redesign_note: The logging redesign (.kiro/specs/logging-redesign) split the public logging
headers so log.hpp/log_format.hpp/log_system.hpp no longer pull <format> or
<filesystem> and hold to the default budget (log.hpp CI ~491 ms).
A design review of the PIMPLs then reverted them in favor of readable classes
(see the PR discussion):
- file_sink.hpp: stores paths as std::string (UTF-8) instead of
std::filesystem::path, so the header needs no <filesystem>/<memory>;
<filesystem> stays in file_sink.cpp. Measured ~172 ms self-parse locally,
no <format>/<filesystem> pulled -> held to the default, no override.
- backend.hpp: a plain class (not PIMPL) whose std::thread / std::mutex /
std::condition_variable members and owned std::vector<unique_ptr<>> must
be complete in the header; those pull <format> on libstdc++ and cannot be
forward-declared. Its ONLY consumer (logger.cpp) already includes all of
those headers for its synchronous backend, so a PIMPL would not reduce
that TU's real build time (measured: PIMPL vs plain-class logger TU
frontend ~907 vs ~900 ms, within noise). Rather than relocate code purely
to satisfy the per-header metric, backend.hpp carries a documented
override. Its self-parse (~565 ms local, method bodies live in
backend.cpp) scales to roughly the pre-PIMPL CI figure (~3022 ms avg);
the override below adds the usual ~40% headroom. Re-measure on the CI
Build-time budget job summary and tighten if the actual figure is lower;
do NOT raise it further to hide a real regression (AGENTS.md / ADR 0005).

control owner / renderer / resampler / voice kernel / bus / spatial /
scheduler sources, and 13 Catch2 test translation units -- plus the private
vendored miniaudio C unit. Every AUDIO PUBLIC HEADER stays well under the

Catch2 test TU parses ~2.5-3.5 s of <catch2> headers, and 13 new audio test
TUs add real, permanent summed frontend parse time. This is the same
'total scales with TU count' growth the $comment calls out, not a heavy
include leaking into a header. Measured summed frontend parsing after the
audio reconciliation: 145.1 s locally (pinned clang-18, linux-clang-
development). Raise the aggregate from 120 s to 170 s (~17 % headroom over
the local 145.1 s). Per-header limits are UNCHANGED. Re-measure on the CI
Build-time budget job summary and tighten toward the observed figure; do NOT
raise further to mask a real regression (ADR 0005 / AGENTS.md).
